items.t: Crop model 11.68m bales vs USDA 13.18m (-11%), driven by Texas abandonment of 51% vs USDA's 34% on drought and poor ratings.
Watch: West Texas-Kansas-Oklahoma (regrowth, insurance adjusters in fields, harvest delays); San Joaquin Valley (SJV) (harvest delays); American Pima (AP) (harvest delays).
25% of US acres contracted as of 2026-10-31 vs 17% a year ago and a 16% five-season average; Texas 36%. More of the crop is priced early, leaving less grower selling for later.
Export sales (week 15) project 12.43 m bales vs USDA 12.30 (+1%); commitments +15% vs a year ago. Outlook above USDA's 12.30 m bales.

India's crop looks like 21.0 m bales on the desk model (USDA 23.5) after the driest June–September in its main cotton districts since at least 1991. With the import duty waived to 2026-12-31 India imports about 4.5 m bales (5.3 m if the waiver runs all season) vs USDA's 3.3 m. US cotton to India: 0.9–1.4 m bales against 0.29 m committed, so 0.6–1.1 m of new US sales are still to come. Counting the Brazilian, African and Australian cotton India takes from other buyers, US exports gain about 0.4 m bales in the desk base and 1.0 m in the bearish (big-crop, lower-price) case; in the desk's simulated balance sheet (crop and exports drawn together, India's duty path included) base exports are 12.8 m vs USDA 12.3, ending stocks 2.6 m (bullish 1.5, bearish 3.9; USDA 3.70), and 86% of runs end below USDA. At today's prices more of this demand gets booked. History says the market prices this through what USDA reports by February–March: if USDA's March US stocks/use reaches the desk base, May, May/Jul (-0.54) and Jul/Dec (+5.36) are all cheap (see Price and spreads); Mar/May (-1.48) has stayed a carry outside world-shortage years.
Desk base case 2026/27 ending stocks 2.60 vs USDA 3.70 (stocks/use 18.3% vs 27.0%); bearish 3.93, bullish 1.50.

May is 80.62. Simulating every combination of crop, exports, India's duty path and historical fit, May averages 98 in February–March (68–147, 10th–90th percentile), with a 69% chance it trades 90 or higher by mid-March and 40% that it trades 78 or lower first. Merchants' shorts are 47% of world exports, the most at this time of year since 2010/11; in heavily hedged seasons May rose 13% on average. Fair value in February–March, when USDA's numbers settle: if USDA's March US stocks/use reaches the desk base (18%), May is worth 90–98, May/Jul +0.2 to +1.1 and Jul/Dec +9 to +11; on USDA's 27.0% they are about 77, -0.6 and +2. Today's prices imply a March number near 25% (May) and 23% (Jul/Dec). Mar/May -1.48 has stayed a carry outside world-shortage years. Open interest has already moved forward: May and Jul hold 123k lots, a record for this date since 2000 (median 31k; 35% of the total vs 20%), so less rolls out of Dec and hedge-lifting as mills fix lands in May and Jul. Downside is limited by who sells: growers are well hedged and can hold cotton in the 55¢ loan, producer fixations are modest and merchants are hedged, so funds are the main seller, against 40k lots mills still have to fix; with a book this size May's worst drop to mid-March has averaged -6% (about 76; worst 71).
